key_insight: CottonLeafVision shows that pretrained deep learning models can be adapted to accurately classify cotton leaf diseases from images, helping make plant disease detection faster and more reliable. The framework also emphasizes explainability and robustness, making predictions easier to trust in real-world farming settings.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of identifying cotton leaf diseases early and accurately from images, which is important for preventing crop loss and protecting agricultural productivity.
method: Evaluates multiple pretrained CNN architectures, including DenseNet201, InceptionV3, and VGG19, on a public cotton leaf disease image dataset.
Compares model performance to identify a strong deep learning baseline for cotton disease classification.
Focuses on building an explainable and robust framework suitable for practical agricultural use.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper demonstrates how transfer learning can be applied effectively to a specialized image classification task with limited domain data. It is useful for anyone building trustworthy computer vision systems for agriculture or other real-world detection problems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing input leaf images flowing into pretrained CNN models and output disease labels
Model comparison bar chart for DenseNet201, InceptionV3, and VGG19 performance
Example leaf images with predicted disease classes and highlighted visual explanations
Icon-based summary of accuracy, robustness, and explainability
paper_title: CottonLeafVision: An Explainable and Robust Deep Learning Framework for Cotton Leaf Disease Classification
paper_authors: Rafi Ahamed, Md. Abir Rahman, Tasnia Tarannum Roza, Munaia Jannat Easha, Md. Asif Khan
